They all leave the triangles through E and F, which share the top at 1.00, while C scores 0.75 and D 0.25; the endpoints themselves score 0." width="100%"} Ordinary betweenness counts shortest paths between every pair of nodes. Subset betweenness (Brandes, 2008) only counts paths that start in `sources=` and end in `targets=`, so it answers a focused question: which nodes carry the traffic from *these* origins to *those* destinations? Examples are the junctions between residential areas and business districts, or the proteins linking a set of receptors to a set of transcription factors. "Shortest" follows `shortest_path()`: hops, or total weight on a weighted graph. Scaling follows NetworkX: raw values by default (halved on undirected graphs, since each path is seen from both ends), or divided by `(n - 1)(n - 2)` with `normalized=True`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [sources]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Starting nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. [targets]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Destination nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, divide by `(n - 1)(n - 2)`. Default is `False`, as in NetworkX. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to measure path length by edge weight. If `None` (default), follows the graph. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store scores in. If `None` (default), uses `"betweenness_centrality_subset"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the scores as a node attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping node IDs to scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node does not exist, or weights are used and one is negative. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a path A-B-C-D-E, traffic from A to C only passes through B, so D gets no credit: ::: {#45529710 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E")]) ) scores = path.betweenness_centrality_subset(["A"], ["C"], return_dict=True) {path.get_label_from_id(n): s for n, s in sorted(scores.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 0.0, 'B': 0.5, 'C': 0.0, 'D': 0.0, 'E': 0.0} ``` ::: :::
